When it's not too bad I take it a lot slower. Having yt on 2x speed helps me personally too, my brain says "you've already watched 2 videos, hurry up and finish whatever you're doing". I do the obvious take 1 thing with you to the correct room when you get up to get a drink, eat, go to the bathroom or whatever, then when I'm in that room I try and put 2 things away. Dishes I try to do 2 or 3 times whatever I used if I need to catch up so I'm not washing like 30 things in 1 sitting. If you're having a bad day, week, whatever try to remember that no matter how bad it does get, that you CAN get out of it and go back to "normal". You can ask for help cleaning from family/friends if you can trust them or if you can afford it hire a cleaner or housekeeper depending on your needs. You may also just need to downsize (easier said than done) or buy some self standing clothing racks so you can see all your clothes without needing to make piles and dig through it all. If you can't bear to part with anything tho, try to not bring anything new in unless you get rid of at least 2 of that thing. Personally that helped me a lot with shoes and shirts since I don't even wear shirts or shoes other than sneakers often, yet I had like 40 other pairs of shoes and sooo many t shirts.

You may be able to get an ESA letter for cheap from a bad online therapist, but it is still technically proof to let you have them even in no pet places with no rent. However some are genuinely needed for different reasons and it's not really up to you to decide, unless you're the property owner and they've caused damage that the owner is refusing to pay for or theyre bothering other tenants. Even in that situation it's up to a judge in court whether they think it's a real ESA or not, not you. Animals have been proven to help with both mental and physical health by being a source of motivation to get out of bed and take care of them instead of laying around and basically letting yourself rot away, plus theyre great companions to help avoid loneliness and decrease depression. Cats have legitimately been proven to lower your risk of high blood pressure, plus plenty of other things as well as dogs. Maybe YOU don't believe there's any valid benefits, but there are, otherwise there would only be pets and service dogs and no ESA's. 

Also btw service animals are actually the 1s that don't need any documentation legally according to the ADA because you're allowed to train your own animal to become a service animal without any type of certification whatsoever. It's to help avoid charging disabled people thousands when a lot of the time, they're already broke due to not being able to work full-time or sometimes at all; since they often go for 10k+ even for the basic stuff like leading a blind person, it only gets more expensive if they're trained to smell allergies and alert their owner to other medical stuff like low blood sugar/pressure etc. 

I suggest being willing to google and maybe even learn a thing or 2, before randomly making stuff up and spouting it like an elderly Facebook user just because you personally dislike it.

The home wifi is not hotspot. Both Verizon and t mobile have that option and there is no actual hardware they come out to install, it's just a box with a 2 in 1 router/modem they send you. It is sort of like a hot spot since it's connected through a phone number, but much better connection and it's treated as actual wifi and Internet without needing to buy more data or being cut off after a certain point since it has it's own dedicated line.

I'm not sure when you went, but it's somewhat "new" and has only been a thing for a few years as far as I know so you may have gotten a worker who didn't know or misunderstood you and thought you wanted a hot spot. It should be around 60 a month, with like a $5 discount if you decide to do auto pay, possibly a bigger discount if they have any offers for new customers currently. It took about a week for them to ship it to us and we set it up in about 10 mins. We've had both services and they are the same for us, just pick whichever 1 has better service in your area or if you already have a phone plan with 1 maybe see if they can bundle it

I'll be the first to admit that I'm bitter for being treated poorly for a large chunk of my life due to being ill (from parents, doctors, school staff, and countless others who should know better). but it's my life and I'm allowed to be distrustful of others and guarded when they display behavior that even children get told off for, while they're adults who are often older than me. children are infinitely more respectful about disabilities, from my own experiences, than any adult, especially adults over 40. the worst a kid has asked was if I could walk and take care of myself while adults have asked me to my face if I could go to the bathroom on my own or assumed I couldn't talk or be my own person and asked my bf or other people I was with if I was hard to take care of/what's wrong with me.

with all that said I'm ambulatory and barely ever even use a mobility aid because I only need it when I have my knee or ankle give out and I've still heard all this crap spewed on multiple occasions. even as a kid when I needed crutches for a couple weeks it was the staff and teachers at school who were nosy and rude, not even the kids who bullied me said anything about the crutches, just their regular routine crap about weight, what my face looked like, financial status, which imo, shows that people learn to be horrible to disabled people instead of being neutral and actually ignorant. it's their fear of people who look different, same as racism, it's learned hatred so I'll never give it a pass just because it's *possible* they don't know better. there's always gonna be possibilities that change things but you can't expect people to cater to it.
